claims.text: The AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock has a homogeneous composition.
The feedstock has a fine particle-size distribution and standard additive-manufacturing pre-processing conditions.
The proposed processing window uses approximately 100 fs laser pulses, controlled low average power, selected repetition rates, and low volume energy density.
Femtosecond pulses confine energy deposition sufficiently to limit heat diffusion in AlCrFeNiSi.
Femtosecond processing eliminates extended melt-pool formation.
Rapid solidification or quenching can freeze in a nonequilibrium short-range-ordered state.
Femtosecond laser melting of AlCrFeNiSi produces an ultrafine-grained microstructure.
The resulting short-range order and ultrafine grains diminish thermal gradients and residual stresses.
Short-range ordering can enhance strength without sacrificing ductility.
Nonequilibrium short-range order will improve the strength–ductility balance of femtosecond-processed AlCrFeNiSi.
Femtosecond-processed components will have significantly lower residual thermal stress than components made under conventional high-thermal-load conditions.
Lower overall energy input will simplify process control.
Lower overall energy input will minimize defect formation.
Conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing processes generate large melt pools, pronounced thermal gradients, high residual stresses, and degraded mechanical properties.
The proposed approach is applicable to miniature components approximately 5 × 5 × 5 mm³ in size.
Scaling femtosecond pulsed processing to larger components presents substantial challenges.
Processing is to be performed under an inert atmosphere with room-temperature tensile testing and nanoindentation.
The falsification experiment compares femtosecond processing with standard high-energy-density laser processing while holding atmosphere, powder characteristics, and geometry constant.
Residual stress, grain size, short-range order, tensile strength, hardness, and ductility are proposed as the measured response variables.
Failure to reduce residual stress, develop the proposed microstructure, or improve the strength–ductility balance is specified as refuting the hypothesis.
